title: Josh and Chuck's Christmas Extravaganza 2012
summary: Christmas special episode covering Christmas trees (real vs. artificial, care and watering, environmental comparison, history of tree lots), the NORAD Santa tracking tradition, eggnog history and George Washington's recipe, the WPIX Yule Log, the history of Dr. Seuss's How the Grinch Stole Christmas and its 1966 TV special, mistletoe kissing lore, the Dutch Saint Nicholas and Black Pete, and a reading of The Elves and the Shoemaker by the Brothers Grimm. Opens with a promo for the upcoming Stuff You Should Know TV show on the Science Channel and a Brooklyn premiere party.
topics: Stuff You Should Know TV show Science Channel

segments.title: Opening and TV show promo
segments.summary: Hosts promote the Stuff You Should Know TV show premiering January 19 on Science Channel, and a Brooklyn premiere party on January 8 at the Bell House.
topics: Stuff You Should Know TV show

segments.title: Christmas opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts greet listeners for the Christmas episode and joke about their studio heat and glasses.

segments.title: Christmas tree farming and selection
segments.summary: Discussion of the US Christmas tree industry, its size and acreage, top producing states, the time it takes trees to mature, and shearing practices. They also note that artificial pre-decorated trees exist.

segments.title: Christmas tree history
segments.summary: Christmas trees trace to German tradition, with Martin Luther credited with decorating them with candles. Commercial tree lots in the US date to the mid-nineteenth century.

segments.title: Caring for a live Christmas tree
segments.summary: Advice to cut an inch off the trunk and keep the tree watered, roughly a gallon per day, with a stand sized to the trunk diameter (a quart or liter per inch of diameter).

segments.title: Artificial vs. real trees and environmental impact
segments.summary: History of artificial trees dating to the nineteenth century. Discussion of a 2009 Montreal study saying an artificial tree must be reused for more than twenty years to be greener than a real tree, and of the artificial tree maker's claim that its product is greener.

segments.title: NORAD tracks Santa
segments.summary: The 1955 Sears-style department store error that listed the Continental Air Defense Command hotline as Santa's number, the start of the NORAD Santa tracking tradition, and the FAA's role since 2006.

segments.title: Eggnog origins and name
segments.summary: Eggnog traced to medieval posset, the arrival of eggnog in America with Captain John Smith, its popularity in America versus England, and competing origins for the name, including 'egg and grog' and 'noggin'.

segments.title: George Washington's eggnog recipe and safety
segments.summary: Reading George Washington's eggnog recipe from Mount Vernon records, with a conversion to commercial eggnog. Discussion of FDA egg content rules for store eggnog and the use of pasteurized eggs.

segments.title: Judge Garnett eggnog anecdote
segments.summary: A 1900 Good Housekeeping story about Judge Garnett of Matthews County, Virginia, and his father drinking eggnog while a house burned.

segments.title: WPIX Yule Log
segments.summary: Origin of the WPIX Yule Log in 1966 under programming director Fred Thrower, its move to high definition in 2004, and availability online.

segments.title: How the Grinch Stole Christmas
segments.summary: Dr. Seuss's origin of the Grinch, its 1957 publication, the 1966 CBS TV special directed with Chuck Jones, Max the dog, Boris Karloff's narration, Thurl Ravenscroft's singing of 'You're a Mean One, Mister Grinch' and June Foray's uncredited role, the Grinch family letter, and the TBS broadcast run.

segments.title: Mistletoe traditions
segments.summary: Mistletoe kissing customs, including taking a berry for each kiss, the luck and marriage superstitions, ancient Viking fertility and truce associations, and burning mistletoe to predict marriage.

segments.title: Dutch Saint Nicholas and Black Pete
segments.summary: Sinterklaas-style Saint Nicholas as the Dutch Santa Claus, with his helper Black Pete who would whip naughty children.

segments.title: Reading: The Elves and the Shoemaker
segments.summary: Hosts read the Brothers Grimm tale The Elves and the Shoemaker as their annual Christmas reading.

segments.title: Holiday sign-off
segments.summary: No listener mail this week. Hosts send holiday greetings to listeners and families and sign off.
